title: Croquet
native: Croquet (from the French jeu de mail)
summary: A lawn game in which wooden balls are driven with a long-handled mallet through small iron hoops set in the grass and on to a striped peg. It grew out of older mallet-and-ball games of France and the British Isles and became a favourite of garden parties and clubs.
howToPlay: Press behind the ball and pull back like drawing a mallet: the dotted line shows the path.
Let go to strike. A longer pull is a harder stroke.
Roll the ball gently between the legs of a white hoop to run it; a ball struck too fast skims through for nothing.
Finish at the striped peg for the biggest score. Ten strokes make a round.
rules: The pull length sets the strength and the dotted guide shows the line.
A ball that crosses a hoop slowly enough runs it and keeps rolling.
A ball that strikes a leg of a hoop bounces away.
The four hoops are worth 2, 2, 3 and 3 points; the striped peg is worth 5.
heritageNote: Played on the lawns of Ireland and Britain since the 1800s, with roots in the French mallet game jeu de mail. Clubs in many countries keep the sport alive.
